what: the front page's intro (the site's own voice)
drafted_by: Claude, from Doug's frame (2026-10-07: 'the Law basically has two lenses -- the OT lens where it was established and the NT lens where it was fulfilled'; 'the greatest commandments ... needs to factor in prominently'; 'Matthew 5:17 is the bridge to fulfillment')

objections: Secular academic, Jewish readers of the Hebrew Bible in mind, and Lutheran / Reformed / Baptist / Wesleyan / Pentecostal / Catholic / Orthodox / biblical-theological alike: 'the New Testament speaks of it, in its own word, as fulfilled' uses 'fulfilled' outside quotation, in the site's own voice. 'In its own word' does not cure it: neither Matthew 5:17 ('to fulfill them', where 'them' is the Law or the Prophets) nor Romans 13:10 ('love is the fulfillment of the law') says the Law itself is fulfilled. The sentence turns two verses into a claim that the Law is fulfilled, which is the very thing traditions dispute and Jewish readers do not accept. Fix: say only 'where the New Testament speaks of it' and let the two quotations carry 'fulfill' and 'fulfillment'. No sentence outside a quotation now says the Law is fulfilled, ended, binding or superseded.

Against the texts: 'the two commandments Jesus calls the greatest' does not match Matthew 22:38-40 exactly. Matthew 22:38 calls only the first 'the first and greatest commandment'; the second 'is like it'. Mark 12:29-31 calls the first 'the most important' and the second 'the second', and then says 'No other commandment is greater than these'. Only Mark 12:31 comes near calling both greatest. Fix: quote Mark 12:31 as Jesus's own words rather than paraphrasing it as 'calls the greatest'.

Biblical-theological (literary) and secular academic: 'two lenses the texts themselves give' attributes to the texts a two-lens frame that no verse gives (nothing in Deuteronomy 4:44 or the New Testament verses says the NT is a lens on the Law); the order Old Testament then New Testament, with 'seen through', reads the Old Testament as something viewed through the New. Fix: 'in two parts', a plain description of the page.
Against the texts: 'where it was given': Deuteronomy 4:44 says 'set before the Israelites', not 'given'. Changed to 'set out'.

Against the texts: Matthew 5:17 was quoted as 'I have not come to abolish them, but to fulfill them' with 'them' left without its antecedent ('the Law or the Prophets'), so it read as about the Law alone. The full verse is now quoted, word for word.

Secular academic and Jewish-reader-minded: 'At its head stand' states a ranking inside the Law as the site's claim, and 'it joins wisdom in the words' asserts that 'His commandments' in Ecclesiastes 12:13 are the Law and that the verse joins it to wisdom; the verse says neither. Fix: 'Set first here' describes the page's order, and 'the page meets Wisdom at Ecclesiastes 12:13' states the page's link rather than what the verse means.
The Note passes: it takes no side, lists the disputes, and uses none of the barred words. No change.

final_note: the reviewer's intro, with 'opening at Matthew 5:17' added by Claude as a description of the page's order

John 15:5 is quoted only in its own words, and "proving yourselves to be My disciples" (John 15:8) is not used in either line. The pairing of John 15 with Galatians 5 is by the word, not by a claim in the site's voice.

Romans 7:4: neutral as the cell stands, because only "in order that we might bear fruit to God" is shown and the clause "you also died to the law" is not used in either line. Lutheran and Reformed readers could read it beside Galatians 5:23 ("no law") as a law-and-gospel statement, but no line draws that link. concepts.name: The Father, the Son or the Lord, and the Spirit named together
concepts.why: Academic and Jewish-aware reader: only Matthew 28:19 says 'Father' and 'Son'; 1 Corinthians 12:4-6, 2 Corinthians 13:14, Ephesians 4:4-6, Jude and Titus say 'Lord'/'God'/'Jesus Christ', so the name says more than most of its passages. The new name says only what they say.

concepts.name: The LORD is One; there is no other
concepts.why: Academic/Jewish reader: Deuteronomy 4:35 and Isaiah 44:6 say 'no other'/'no God but Me', not 'One'; Romans 3:30 and James 2:19 say 'one God', not 'the LORD'. The name should cover what all eight say. No passage here says anything about the Son or the Spirit, so none implies a side.

concepts.name: The one God, and Jesus Christ
concepts.why: Biblical-theological and academic reader: only 1 Corinthians 8:6 says 'the Father' and 'one Lord'; 1 Timothy 2:5, John 17:3, Romans 16:27 and Jude 25 say 'one/only God' and 'Jesus Christ' without 'Father' or 'Lord' (Jude says 'our Lord' but of Jesus Christ after 'only God our Savior'). The new name is true to all five and neither equates nor separates God and Jesus Christ, which Trinitarian and non-Trinitarian readers would otherwise read into 'one God, the Father, and one Lord'.

concepts.name: The Word, with God and from the Father
concepts.why: Academic and Reformed/Orthodox reader: 'The Word was with God' is said only by John 1:1-2. John 1:18 does not name the Word, and its 'who is Himself God' renders a Greek reading on which the manuscripts divide (the original arbitrates; the English gloss goes beyond what a neutral label can carry here). Revelation 19:13 says 'the Word of God', not 'with' or 'from', so under the new name it says less than its neighbours. John 1:1-2's note 'the Word was God' is the text's own words and may stay; it is not paired with an answer.

concepts.name: I and the Father are one; the Father is in Me
concepts.why: Name must not say 'one' for passages that say only 'in': John 10:38, 14:9-11 and 17:21 speak of being 'in' each other; only John 10:30 and 17:22 say 'one'. Matthew 11:27 speaks of mutual knowing, neither 'one' nor 'in'; it belongs under 'My Father' (concept 7) if kept at all. Keeping John 17:21-22 beside John 10:30 is the texts' own repeated word 'one' and is not set to explain it.

concepts.name: My Father and My God
concepts.why: Name must not set itself as the answer to concept 6 and must not say 'greater' for passages that do not: only John 14:28 says 'greater'. Mark 13:32, John 5:19, 20:17, 1 Corinthians 11:3 and 15:28 each speak of the Son in relation to the Father or God, as 'My Father and My God' (John 20:17) does for all. 'The Father is greater than I' stays as the John 14:28 note, in the texts' words. Matthew 11:27 ('entrusted to Me by My Father') may be moved here from concept 6.

Academic reader: Acts 2:33 says 'the promised Holy Spirit' received from the Father, but not 'Advocate' nor 'Spirit of truth', so the passage does not say what the name says. John 15:26 ('whom I will send ... who proceeds from the Father') and 16:13-15 are the texts' words and are listed without comment, so neither the Catholic nor the Orthodox reader finds a side taken.

concepts.name: God's Spirit
concepts.why: Jewish reader of the Hebrew Bible and academic reader: 'Your Holy Spirit' is Psalm 51:11 only; Isaiah 63:10-11 also says 'Holy', but Genesis 1:2, Psalm 139:7, Ezekiel 36:27, Joel 2:28 say 'Spirit of God', 'Your/My Spirit'. Isaiah 48:16's speaker is disputed, and 'accompanied by His Spirit' settles a Hebrew ambiguity (it can read 'and His Spirit has sent me') one way; placed beside the Father and the Son it reads as a proof text. Genesis 1:2 'Spirit of God' is the passage's rendering of a word that can also be 'wind'; it stays because the passage text says it.

Hebrews 1:3 note quotes 'the radiance of God's glory and the exact representation of His nature', which is not about the right hand and which Unitarian and Trinitarian readers take in opposite directions; the note should be the passage's right-hand clause, 'He sat down at the right hand of the Majesty on high.' (that passage says 'the Majesty on high', not 'God', which is fine as a circumlocution the Jewish reader knows). Mark 16:19 is the disputed longer ending; keep it only if the site shows that elsewhere.

secondary_or_links: Order: do not place concept 6 ('one') directly before concept 7 ('greater'), nor 3-4 ('one God') directly before 5-6; arrange so neither is read as the answer to the other (for example by passage order or alternating). A Lutheran, Reformed or Catholic reader would read adjacent pairing as an argument.

Concept 7 note on John 5:19 quotes only 'the Son can do nothing by Himself, unless He sees the Father doing it'; the same verse continues 'For whatever the Father does, the Son also does.' Quote both sentences so the note is not half of what the verse says.

'The Father -> sends the Spirit (John 14:26, John 15:26, Galatians 4:6)': John 15:26 says 'whom I will send ... from the Father' and John 14:26 says 'the Father will send in My name'. Relabel 'The Spirit -> sent (John 14:26, John 15:26, Galatians 4:6)' so neither the Catholic nor the Orthodox reader finds the sender decided.

'Honor the Son -> honor the Father (John 5:23, 1 John 2:23)': 1 John 2:23 says 'has the Father', not 'honor'. Drop 1 John 2:23 from this line, or relabel the line 'the Son and the Father: honor (John 5:23), having (1 John 2:23)'.

'The Spirit -> Abba! Father! (Romans 8:15-16, Galatians 4:6)': Romans 8:15 says 'we cry, Abba, Father' by the Spirit; only Galatians 4:6 has the Spirit crying. Relabel 'Abba! Father! -> by the Spirit'.
'Access to the Father -> by one Spirit (Ephesians 2:18)': the verse says 'through Him ... by one Spirit'; add 'through Him' so the Son is not left out of the line.

Link 'Father, Son And Holy Spirit -> Law/Wisdom': no passage here speaks of Law or Wisdom; the link would imply the Word is Wisdom, a reading some readers hold and some deny. Drop it unless a passage shared by both themes is shown.

Do not use the word 'Trinity' anywhere on the page; the theme name and the passages' own words are enough. The other links (Spirit, Messiah/Christology, Children of God, Church, Creation, Prophetic Word & Fulfillment, Kingdom, Temple/Presence, Deliverance/Salvation) are acceptable as plain topic links.

'Satan before the LORD' is the texts' own wording in Job, Zechariah 3:1-2 and 'before our God' in Revelation 12:10, and the notes on Zechariah 3:1 and Revelation 12:10 still carry the word 'accuse'.

concepts.name: Commanding the unclean spirits
concepts.why: Pentecostal/Baptist/Reformed/academic: 'cast out' says more than Luke 10:17 ('submit') and Acts 19:13-16 (an attempt that fails, the spirit answers and the sons of Sceva are overcome); the name also reads as a standing claim about casting out today. The new name uses the texts' verbs (wage war, fight the good fight) and fits all six passages.

concepts.name: Deliver us, keep them, guard you
concepts.why: academic/Lutheran/Orthodox/Catholic: the Greek tou ponerou in Matthew 6:13, John 17:15 and 2 Thessalonians 3:3 can be 'the evil one' or 'evil'; the name 'from the evil one' rests on the BSB's reading and settles in one translation's favour what the original leaves open, and it is not said by Matthew 26:41 or Luke 22:31-32 at all. The verbs deliver / keep / guard (and 'protects' in 1 John 5:18) are the texts' words and cover all six passages without choosing; the notes (exact to the BSB) can stay.

concepts.name: Overcome, conquer, crush
concepts.why: academic/Wesleyan/Pentecostal: 'You have overcome the evil one' is 1 John 2:13-14 only; 1 John 4:4 says 'overcome them' (the spirits of the antichrist, not the evil one), Revelation 12:11 'conquered him', Romans 16:20 is a future promise that God 'will crush Satan', and Luke 10:19 is authority given, so the name asserts a present, completed victory by believers that three passages do not say. concepts.name: The devil destroyed and hurled down

The new name is the texts' words (destroy, hurled down) and takes no side on when the fall happened or on the end of the devil beyond what Revelation 20:10 says.

secondary_or_links: No change needed: secondary concepts and links use the texts' own words and take no side on the satan title, exorcism today, territorial spirits or the armor. Optional: Mark 9:29 is in the 'Watch and pray' secondary and its 'and fasting' variant is a manuscript matter, but the BSB reading is quoted exactly, so leave it.

concepts.name: Children of God
concepts.why: Academic/Reformed/Baptist: only 1 John 3:1 says 'called'; Gal 3:26, Phil 2:15, John 11:52 and John 1:12 (the right to become) do not, so 'Called' says more than most of its passages. Plain label in the texts' words fits all six; all notes are exact quotations.

concepts.name: Sons of the LORD, sons of the living God
concepts.why: Academic/Jewish reader: only Hosea 1:10 and Romans 9:26 say 'sons of the living God'; Deuteronomy 14:1 says 'sons of the LORD your God' and Isaiah 43:6 says 'My sons'. The two-part name is in the texts' words and covers all four; notes are exact.

concepts.name: Israel is My firstborn son; I am Israel's Father
concepts.why: Academic/Jewish/Reformed: 'Israel is My firstborn son' is said only by Exodus 4:22; Deuteronomy 32:6, Isaiah 63:16 and 64:8 say 'Father', not son or firstborn; Jeremiah 31:9 says Ephraim is firstborn. The two-quotation name (Exodus 4:22 and Jeremiah 31:9) fits the whole set; notes are exact.

concepts.name: Offspring of God, the son of God
concepts.why: Lutheran/Reformed/Catholic/Baptist: grouping Acts 17 and Luke 3:38 with Malachi 2:10 (addressed to Israelites, 'the covenant of our fathers') and Ephesians 4:6 (set within the one body of the church) under 'We are His offspring' reads as the site asserting that all people are God's children, which Children of God must not decide. Neither passage says 'offspring'. Both stay in the secondary 'One Father' item, where they are in the texts' own words.

concepts.name: Born again, born of God
concepts.why: Academic/Orthodox/Catholic: 'Born of God' alone is said only by John 1:13, 1 John 3:9 and 5:1; John 3:3 and 1 Peter 1:23 say 'born again', James 1:18 and 1 Peter 1:3 say God gave birth / new birth, and John 3:5 says 'water and the Spirit'. The name now covers them without deciding what John 3:5's water is; John 3:5 is kept with its exact quotation and no gloss.

concepts.name: Calling on God as Father
concepts.why: Academic/Orthodox/Catholic: 'Abba' appears only in Galatians 4:6 and Mark 14:36; Matthew 6:9, 1 Peter 1:17, Jeremiah 3:19 and Psalm 89:26 are about calling God 'Father'. The plain label fits all six. Galatians 4:6 and Mark 14:36 are set side by side with no comment on the Father and the Son; that is acceptable.

concepts.name: Heirs and the inheritance
concepts.why: Academic/Wesleyan/Baptist: 'Heirs of God and co-heirs with Christ' is Romans 8:17 alone; Galatians 3:29, Titus 3:7, Ephesians 3:6, James 2:5 and 1 Peter 1:4 speak of heirs by the promise, fellow heirs, inheriting the kingdom, an inheritance. The plain label covers all; notes are exact. The Romans 8:17 wording stays as the first item's note.

concepts.name: God is a Father
concepts.why: Academic/Jewish/Orthodox: 'I will be a Father to you' is said only in 2 Corinthians 6:18 (and in the form 'I will be his Father' in 2 Samuel 7:14 and 1 Chronicles 17:13); Revelation 21:7 says 'I will be his God'; Psalms 68:5 and 103:13 are descriptions, not promises. The plain label fits all six; notes are exact.

concepts.name: Sons of God, sons of the Most High
concepts.why: Academic/Lutheran/Catholic: 'sons of your Father in heaven' is Matthew 5:45 only; Matthew 5:9 and Luke 20:36 say 'sons of God', Luke 6:35 says 'sons of the Most High'. The new name is in the texts' words and covers all four; notes are exact.

concepts.name: Discipline as a father disciplines his son
concepts.why: Academic/Wesleyan/Reformed: 'the one He loves' is said only by Hebrews 12:6 and Proverbs 3:12; Deuteronomy 8:5 and Hebrews 12:9 say a father disciplines (without 'loves'). The new name is the thought all four share; notes are exact.

concepts.name: Jesus' brothers
concepts.why: Academic/Baptist/Catholic/Orthodox: 'firstborn among many brothers' is Romans 8:29 only; Hebrews 2:11, Matthew 12:50 and John 20:17 speak of brothers without 'firstborn', and Matthew 12:50 also says sister. Plain label covers all; Romans 8:29's wording stays in its note. John 20:17 ('My Father and your Father, My God and your God') is left uncommented and not set against any other passage, which is correct.

secondary_or_links: 'Born of God -> overcomes the world ()' and 'Born of God -> loves one another ()' have no references; nothing without scripture. Cite 1 John 5:4 and 1 John 4:7 (checked against the full text) or drop both.

'Children of God -> children of the devil (Matthew 13:38)': Matthew 13:38 speaks of 'sons of the kingdom' and 'sons of the evil one', not 'children of God'; the pairing in those words is 1 John 3:10. Lutheran/Reformed/Wesleyan/Baptist: as it stands the arrow imports a reading of who is whose child that the cited verse does not state.

'One Father -> in heaven (Malachi 2:10, Matthew 23:9, Ephesians 4:6)': only Matthew 23:9 says 'in heaven'. Relabel as 'One Father' with the three references (no arrow), or keep 'in heaven' with Matthew 23:9 alone.

'Now children of God -> not yet revealed (Romans 8:18, Romans 8:23)': 'not yet been revealed' is 1 John 3:2 (the first concept's passage); Romans 8:18 says the glory is to be revealed and 8:23 says adoption is awaited. Add 1 John 3:2 to the references.

'Children of the flesh -> children of the promise (Romans 9:8, Galatians 4:28)': acceptable as the texts' own contrast; keep the label strictly in those two verses' words so it is not read as deciding Israel and the church.
